Lane `check/M0-s-01-close-s2` ran under Opus 5.5 in Claude Code in a claude.ai cloud container on 2026-10-11, from
05:20 to about 05:35 UTC. The machine check printed `linux:Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz:4cpu:16gib`, as the
brief says, and Node was v24.12.0. The seat is an implementer-side closing checker. It wrote no part of the round: the
round's author was `build/M0-s-01-fix-s2` (L-0402; choices row C-0306). The round was opened by the session
(docs/M0-FIX-QUEUE.md Q23), not by a failed check of the item.

How the seat worked:

* It changed no file of the item. It wrote this file, rows N-11 – N-16 of `checks/M0-s-01-notes.md`, its CLEAN-ROOM
  row, its two landed records and its lane-log lines. It ran no git command.
* It planned its probes and its 25 targeted mutants from the two failing lines and from the code
  (`tools/landed/landed.mjs`, `verify.mjs`, `landed.test.mjs`), before it read anything of the author's self-check. The
  author's lane lines showed up in the resume grep and named mutant ids only. The seat did not use them as evidence or
  as a map, and it did not open the author's mirror.
* Its own mirror was `scratchpad/waves/check-M0-s-01/close-s2/m/plat`: a tar copy of `plat/` without `node_modules`,
  `dist` or `*.tsbuildinfo`, with `node_modules` linked to the tree's. Each mutant was restored after its run, and
  `diff -rq` of `tools/landed` against the tree printed nothing at the end. The mirror's probe files and its re-landed
  M0-s-01 record were reset or removed.
* Tree runs used `--maxWorkers=$W` from `tools/test_budget.py` (it printed 1). Mutants ran one at a time with
  `--maxWorkers=1`. No timing was taken or judged.

## Verdict: PASS. Both failing lines are fixed, and there is no new blocker

Four mutants survived on promises the round states: A6, A4, B6 and V3 (§3 below). None of them is equivalent. For each
one, the seat's own probe CONFIRMED that the code behaves as promised on today's tree. What is missing is a test that
would catch a later regression, and two of the four (A6, A4) would fail safe even if the regression happened. Following
N-45 and the S1 precedent (`checks/M0-s-01-s1.md`, survivors MA5, MD1 and MD14), the seat filed them as KI notes
N-11 – N-14 (M4). Read strictly, the brief's sentence "a survivor on a stated promise … stays a BLOCKER" would make A6
(the first §2 row accepted) a failing line. If the session reads it that way, A6 is the line to return, and N-11 names
its few-line fix.
